note: Batch-one Llama-3-8B on Graviton3 Arm CPU: at 64 cores, optimized Q4_0_8_8 versus standard Q4_0 reports 570.9 versus 190.4 prefill tokens/s and 46.8 versus 46.0 decode tokens/s. Phase throughput and a Q4_0 comparator do not establish lower full-request CPU-seconds, complete Q4_K_M artifact bytes, peak RAM, or held-out multistep quality.

title: Evaluating large language model compression: a comparative analysis on state-of-the-art models across diverse hardware platforms
note: Cross-platform compression study reports that Qwen3-1.7B GPTQ on a CPU-only laptop failed to produce a token after approximately three hours while an uncompressed variant approached four tokens/s. Backend and format differ from GGUF Q4_K_M; the case illustrates that smaller storage can fail the execution gate.

title: Sandwich: Joint Configuration Search and Hot-Switching for Efficient CPU LLM Serving
note: Across five x86 and Arm CPU platforms, authors report mean 2.01 times end-to-end speedup against tested serving systems, including sequential single-sequence request tests. The precision and system comparators differ from same-base Q4_K_M; no complete-byte, CPU-second, peak-RAM and held-out quality conjunction.

title: DECA: A Near-Core LLM Decompression Accelerator Grounded on a 3D Roofline Model
note: A simulated 56-core Xeon-like HBM design with near-core decompression and an ISA extension reports up to four times faster compressed GeMM and 1.6 to 1.9 times faster next-token generation than software. This is a hardware simulation, not commodity CPU full-request or quality evidence.

title: SFMP: Fine-Grained, Hardware-Friendly and Search-Free Mixed-Precision Quantization for Large Language Models
note: Block-wise 2/3/4-bit rates, row and column Fisher reordering, and a unified CUDA kernel are reported with public perplexity and short-task scores. GPU format and quality metrics do not establish a complete CPU GGUF package, full-request CPU-seconds, peak RAM, or sealed multistep success.

title: SoftWater: Class-aware rate allocation for softmax quantization
note: Class-aware output-head bit allocation reports 59 of 60 matched-rate KL wins over WaterSIC and a tied Llama-3.2-1B model-size reduction from 737.3 to 297.0 MiB with a two-bit body. Its comparator retains an FP16 head and its format is not GGUF; no same-base Q6_K-to-Q4_K CPU four-gate result.

title: Softmax Reparameterization for Output-Head Quantization
note: Uses exact linear-softmax row-shift equivalence to improve W4 output-head quality. Packed A10G measurements are GPU and warm; tied Phi resident weights rise when a separate W4 head is added. No Q6_K-to-Q4_K GGUF CPU four-gate or sealed multistep result.

title: ARCHead: Activation-Metric Residual Correction for Large Language Model Output Heads
note: Packed INT4 plus residual correction reduces persistent Qwen3-8B head state from reported BF16 1188 MB to 304 MB with near-parity perplexity. Head-only denominator and GPU PyTorch/Triton path do not establish a smaller already-Q6_K complete GGUF, CPU peak RAM, full-request CPU-seconds, or sealed multistep quality.

title: AlignQuant: Tile-Aligned Mixed-Precision Quantization for Efficient LLM Generation
note: GPU tile-aligned W4/W8 precision with phase-aware calibration and prefill/decode kernels. Internal 128/512 A100 control reports all-W4 4.01 bits per weight, 138.96 tokens/s and 2.17 GiB peak versus its mixed default 5.61 bits, 132.28 tokens/s and 2.72 GiB. Gains against BF16 do not establish a Q4 resource win; no CPU GGUF four-gate or sealed multistep result.

title: Beyond 4 Bits: Data-Centric Post-Training Quantization and Recovery
note: At about 2.26 to 2.31 effective bits per weight, its best separate calibration recipes give Phi-4-mini BF16 versus YAQA means of 71.0 versus 63.3 on QA and 73.2 versus 37.4 on generation; Llama-3.1-8B also loses generation. Calibration domains change generation substantially. No Q4_K_M CPU GGUF, complete-byte, peak-RAM, full-request CPU, or sealed benign multistep result.

title: Beyond Accuracy: How Quantization Affects Coding Agents
note: Across 115 OJBench problems and three seeds, 4-bit AWQ shifted Qwen2.5-Coder-7B solves from 17 one-shot and 10 loop-based under BF16 to zero one-shot and 25 loop-based. Final accuracy comparisons were not significant after Holm correction, but solve paths shifted at the problem level. End-to-end latency, CPU-seconds, and peak memory were not measured.

title: The Structure of Quantization Damage in LLMs: Why the Next Bit Should Be Spent Globally
note: At matched first-order weight-only precision budgets, global group-128 granularity beat locally restored layers by 21 to 52 CORE points for all eight compatible tested models. Local ranking used evaluation outcomes as an oracle. Complete packaged bytes, CPU peak RAM, full-request CPU-seconds, and sealed multistep quality were not established.

title: On the Fragility of Tasks under Composition: Implicit Budgeting in Language Models
note: Eight models and eight datasets combine independent questions into one prompt and grade each answer. Measured-fragility batching saved 43% generated tokens per task at +0.6 percentage points mean accuracy over seven datasets excluding AIME; a predictor saved 31.0% on that aggregate. Section 4.2's claim of predictor losses at most 0.5 point on every dataset conflicts with Table 1's Claude Opus 5 GPQA row: 2.0-point loss for 0.5% output-token saving. The measured arm needs repeated per-task trials; the predictor uses a separate Qwen3 Embedding 8B plus training trials. Results do not address dependent multistep integration, Q4_K_M 1.5B CPU, complete deployed bytes, process/cgroup peak RAM, or full-request CPU-seconds.

title: Measuring and Narrowing the Compositionality Gap in Language Models
note: Compositional Celebrities has 8.6k templated two-hop questions. Table 6 reports Davinci-002 with 41.8% both subanswers and final answer correct and 33.4% both subanswers correct but final answer wrong, a 44.4% failure conditional on correct subanswers. Table 1 Bamboogle uses 125 manually judged questions and reports direct 17.6%, chain of thought 46.4%, self-ask 57.6%. Older models and factual QA; extra prompt/search and output-token costs are not full-request CPU-seconds. No Q4_K_M compression, complete file, or RAM result.

title: Faith and Fate: Limits of Transformers on Compositionality
note: Executable multiplication, logic-grid, and dynamic-programming tasks; Appendix B reports 500 test examples per task and model. Out-of-domain compound accuracy declines with computation-graph complexity in 2023 model experiments. This does not establish universal impossibility or any result for a local Q4_K_M model, package size, CPU peak RAM, or full-request CPU-seconds.

title: When Structure Is Hidden: Measuring and Diagnosing the Compositional Gap in LLMs
note: Five datasets include 2,000 contracts, 1,319 GSM8K, 1,034 Spider, 164 HumanEval, and 204 FOLIO items. Pass-1 isolated-piece correctness gates conditional gap estimates, so these are not unconditional task success. Qwen2.5-7B Spider eligible n=504: self-derived structure prompt changes gap 25.6% to 33.7%; Llama-3.1-8B eligible n=366: 31.1% to 41.5%. Correct externally supplied structure helps contracts/SQL more than math/logic. Self-structure uses two requests; paper does not report complete CPU bytes/RAM/request cost or Q4_K_M. Intended CoT repeat flag is unused in released code, so baseline repeats cannot establish CoT benefit.

title: Composition Collapse: Stable Factual Knowledge Does Not Imply Compositional Reasoning
note: D4V2 has 390 temporal-chain instances and 2,490 atomic questions; conditional failures are gated on paraphrase-stable atomic and isolated subanswer correctness. Same-base Qwen2.5-7B Table 7 depth-4 residual failure: GRPO 23.4%, answer SFT 63.8%, trace SFT 76.9%; this is a narrow training/task comparison, not unconditional success or CPU deployment evidence. Candidate failure filtering found 70/251 format/scoring artifacts. Seven open 7B-13B models, but no Q4_K_M, complete file/RAM/CPU-seconds, or independent held-out broad multistep quality gate.

title: ClosureBench: A Constructive Benchmark for Compositional Graph Reasoning
note: Constructive graph benchmark with 26 categories. Qwen3-4B LoRA Ein-program arm solves 1,226/1,300 fresh held-out instances and executes on 1,295/1,300, confirmed in released experiments/ein-sft/summary.json after three epochs. These are fresh instances in the same categories and graph sizes 4 to 10, not new program structures. Paper reports direct-answer SFT 59.2%, but §3.4 describes both SFT arms as three epochs while §4.1 associates that answer result with epoch five; matched training budget and direct-answer raw outcome file were not established in this audit. A 600-token syntax specification and external executor are part of the system. No complete CPU package, process/cgroup RAM, full-request CPU-seconds, or Q4_K_M comparison; unreplicated preprint.

title: Train Overcomplete, Deploy Compact: Scaling Recovery Capacity for Structured LLM Pruning
note: Peer-reviewed OverRep study trains a temporary two-block overcomplete recovery module after structured layer pruning and folds it into ordinary projections. Six backbones; controlled FineWeb-Edu subset of 120,000 training and 4,000 test samples; 10 public reasoning and three generation tasks. Table 1 retained performance means pruned-model task mean divided by dense-parent task mean. LLaMA3-3B at 25% pruning: 90.2% versus LoRA 84.7%; at 50%: 72.3% versus RankAdaptor 63.9%. The advertised 5.5- and 8.4-point gains are maxima, not quality parity. Main results concern layer pruning. Figure 3 reports training resource measurements on two RTX 3090 GPUs, not deployed CPU inference. No exact GGUF package, CPU process/cgroup peak or full-request CPU-seconds, Q4_K_M comparator, or sealed dependent-step quality. Code released at https://github.com/mmai-laboratory/OverRep; independent replication not established in this audit.

title: Revisiting Pruning vs Quantization for Small Language Models
note: Five 1B-to-3.8B models in main study and a 0.5B appendix model; seven multilingual perplexity languages and seven public zero-shot downstream tasks. Compares SparseGPT/Wanda 50% and 75% chiefly unstructured sparsity with GPTQ/AWQ INT8 and INT4 relative to FP16; quantization generally better preserves fidelity and task accuracy, with task-specific exceptions. Explicitly assumes no pruning-mask storage overhead and plots effective parameter size from sparsity rather than measuring exported bytes; Table 3 speed figures are theoretical or borrowed. Appendix 2:4 test is on one 1.5B model. Own experiments run on one A100, no CPU GGUF, complete package, peak process/cgroup RAM, full-request CPU-seconds or sealed dependent-step quality. Does not resolve physical width pruning with recovery.

title: StructureBench: A Unified Benchmark Suite for Multi-Scenario Structured Generation Tasks with On-Device Models
note: Peer-reviewed study of 11 on-device 0.5B-to-8B models on 13 structured datasets using prompt-only, Outlines, XGrammar and Guidance. Separates structural validity from conditional semantic correctness and disables retry/fallback. Table 4 Qwen3-0.6B plus XGrammar pattern diagnostics: schema-aligned conditional structural fix 94.8%, conditioned semantic bonus 70.5%; meaning-bound AMR/PDDL/SQL 16.0% and 1.5%; designated Python exception constraint-induced repetition 97.6%. These are heterogeneous pattern summaries, not direct quality forecasts for arithmetic or dependent chains. Grammar can repair format without semantic correctness. No same-base Q4_K_M compression comparison, cold CPU process/cgroup peak, complete package or full-request CPU-seconds.

title: Practical Limits of Lossless Compression for bf16 Transformer LLM Weights, with Companion Measurements on Q4 K Tensors in GGUF Q4 K M Files
note: Primary paper, five complete GGUF Q4_K_M artifacts from bartowski builds. Five-stream transformed archive with zstd-19 reports per-model amortized complete-artifact ratios 1.041 to 1.045, versus 1.022 for whole-file zstd-19. Its 1.076 Q4_K tensor-stream ceiling is confined to a specified within-superblock coder class, not all lossless coding. Single-core Sapphire Rapids decompression is around 110 MB/s; no native fused llama.cpp execution, cold total RAM, or full-request CPU-seconds. Full multi-model inference-sanity sweep is deferred. Adjacent-layer scalar-affine BF16 null uses 250 same-role pairs from two Qwen2.5 models only. The paper's hosted reproduction URL returned 401 Unauthorized during 2026-11-12 audit; raw rows/code were not independently replayed.

title: A Cache-Aware Compression Framework: Deriving the Compression Target and Stopping Rule for Transformers on CPU-Class Hardware
note: Peer-reviewed Whisper-medium Uzbek ASR CPU experiment on one i7-11850H using ONNX Runtime 1.28. Derives per-operator/layer working-set target from effective L3 budget, physically removes functionally similar FFN channels with compensation, then per-output-channel INT8 GPTQ and task-level paired quality stop. Encoder 17.1% channel cut reduces serialized INT8 encoder 300 to 267 MiB; paired 300-utterance WER difference from GPTQ-only -0.0014, 95% CI [-0.0115,+0.0096]. Whole cascade 705 MiB and 4.14-times size reduction is versus FP32, as is six-recording 14,457 to 6,134 ms eight-thread end-to-end wall-time comparison. Separate 1.91-times execution measure covers one encoder forward plus one decoder step. Decoder has no KV cache. Alternative L3 sizes are input scenarios, not other measured machines. A Qwen2.5-0.5B SwiGLU diagnostic found just 0.04% to 0.14% near-collinear channels at the stated threshold, unlike 17.1% for Whisper, and cannot prove a Qwen2.5-1.5B null. Matched-size FLAP WER 0.1838 versus proposed 0.1833 has a paired interval including zero. No native Q4_K_M GGUF, complete installed bytes, cold process/cgroup peak, full-request CPU-seconds, or sealed benign dependent-step LLM quality.

title: CompressionBench: How can your coding agents compress LLMs?
note: Six coding agents each optimize six base-model/storage settings for eight hours, using one H200 NVL per run; 29/36 final artifacts pass independent checks. Saved-package budget includes weights, inference code and tokenizer. Resident model-storage allowance includes persistent reconstructed weights but excludes KV cache, recurrent state and temporary workspace; Appendix A8 separately samples actual peak device memory for two released controls. Lowest-PPL artifact per setting averages 3.4% higher PPL and 77.33% versus 79.56% BF16 mean accuracy across 50 held-out items each of GSM8K, HumanEval and TriviaQA; pass floor is only 80% of BF16 mean, not paired noninferiority. Complete-model feedback reverses 17/79 prior local candidate rankings, and one dense sequence improves PPL as GSM8K drops 88% to 72%. Appendix A6 four fresh eight-hour agent-design repeats all pass verification and have PPL within 0.81% of their original designs, yet the GLM dense-repeat 150-question mean falls from 80.67% to 68.67%, so near-matched PPL does not ensure stable downstream accuracy. Reported speed is warm batch-one decode from first to last of 128 output tokens after a 2048-token prompt, excluded from reward. The 12-GiB dense published release gets 74.6 TPS versus a Sonnet artifact's 16.7 TPS despite the latter's lower PPL and higher mean answer accuracy. GPU 27B/120B/122B parents, not a CPU Q4_K_M complete-byte/cold-RAM/full-request-cost/sealed-dependent-quality four-gate result; unreplicated preprint.

title: AgentCoMa: A Compositional Benchmark Mixing Commonsense and Mathematical Reasoning in Real-World Scenarios
note: Dependent commonsense-selection then math benchmark: 260 expert-written cases, 80 development and 180 test, evaluated on 61 open-weight models. Table 2 displays 16 representative models with mean 80% both-isolated-step success versus 51% composed success. A100/vLLM two-shot greedy inference with up to 2048 generated tokens, not CPU Q4_K_M. Official evaluator pinned at https://github.com/lisaalaz/agentcoma-benchmark/blob/5464e3e7cf7261837876f5ea3f12d477579a68f5/eval.py: check_text is called only for isolated commonsense. Its exact-string delimiter split can raise; the except branch then sets is_correct=0 even when GPT-4o judges the full response correct. Numeric math and composition use accuracy instead; gap is comp_acc minus both_steps_acc. For affected correct isolated commonsense responses this bug lowers both_steps_acc and attenuates a negative gap, but occurrence and magnitude require raw-output rescoring. External diagnostic only, not a complete-byte, cold CPU RAM, full-request CPU-seconds, or sealed same-base quality result.

title: Language model capabilities fail in a shared, predictable order under compression and perturbation
note: Eight BF16 instruction models including Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct undergo four random damage methods plus Wanda, SparseGPT and GPTQ. Sixteen short-answer tasks have 300 evaluation and 40 calibration items each, four answer formats, and a 32-new-token cap. Within-model random-damage versus compression fragility order has median correlation 0.875 across 18 compression cells, but GPTQ order does not transfer across models (median 0.095 across six pairs). A separate preregistered long-form extension has four models, four tasks, and 200 items per task under Gaussian noise and Wanda; only 10/16 task-model positions stay within the target band, below the required 12/16. GSM8K chain-of-thought becomes more fragile under Wanda in three models. At intermediate damage, 83% of repeated-answer errors break the template and 79% of these retain the correct content answer. Short-answer effects cannot predict sealed dependent multistep quality. No native Q4_K_M GGUF, deployed package bytes, cold CPU memory, or full-request CPU-seconds. Unreplicated preprint; alternate primary landing page https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11695.

title: PRISM a diagnostic framework for parametric recall degradation in quantized large language models
note: Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct torchao RTN leak-free fictional-entity multi-hop probes with FP16 output head: two-hop n=160 open-book accuracy FP16/4-bit/3-bit 0.98/0.74/0.15 (Table 8); three-hop n=80 0.912/0.812/0.013 (Table 15); long-context multi-hop n=100 0.75/0.54/0.00 (Table 18). Closed-book accuracy is zero by construction; long-context free-form chain-of-thought has high OTHER rate 0.31 to 0.59. GPU RTX 5060; separate Qwen2.5-7B GGUF sweep offloads all layers to GPU and does not supply the 3B multi-hop numbers. Synthetic template-bound sets and no native CPU Q4_K_M head comparison, complete package bytes, cold process/cgroup peak, or full-request CPU-seconds. Cited per-item/code URL https://github.com/Swa-s-tik/PRISM returned HTTP 404 in the 2026-11-12 audit, preventing independent replay.

title: iGSM synthetic grade-school math generator and evaluator
note: Official pinned generator for the 2024 Physics of Language Models Part 2.1 and 2.2 studies. Pinned commit a1ed1d04600add811beb08b58d9912ed30999642 has a GitHub API committer date of 2025-01-12; source accessed 2026-11-12. Its README describes problem.G as a layered structure graph represented by boolean NumPy matrices, problem.template as a networkx directed dependency graph, a deterministic fix_seed example, and a solution evaluator. These fields permit a prospective test split by dependency topology; the repository itself does not establish such a holdout, disjointness from model pretraining, retained quality under compression, complete GGUF bytes, cold CPU RAM, or full-request CPU-seconds.

title: QPruner: Probabilistic Decision Quantization for Structured Pruning in Large Language Models
note: Physical LLM-Pruner pruning followed by BitsandBytes 4/8-bit layer allocation, Bayesian search and LoftQ recovery, evaluated on NVIDIA L20. Table 1 at 50% LLaMA-7B pruning reports QPruner3 peak memory 16.65 GB and BoolQ 48.37%, versus equally pruned half-precision LLM-Pruner 23.89 GB and 43.76%; unpruned BoolQ is 73.09%. Seven zero-shot commonsense classification benchmarks and 50,000 public Alpaca recovery examples; quantized LoftQ and half-precision LoRA differ in recovery recipe. The paper does not specify the exact measurement stage or process accounting for Table 1 peak memory, so its GPU figure must not be treated as cold CPU total RAM. It does not report complete GGUF bytes, Q4_K_M same-base comparison, full-request CPU-seconds, or sealed dependent-step noninferiority.

title: Quantifying the Stability of Multi-Step Reasoning via Error Amplification
note: Qwen-1.5B task-specific training combines intermediate-step subsampling and 1–4-bit quantization-aware LoRA. Table 1 final-answer Dijkstra 76.2% versus strongest baseline 74.5%, Bellman-Ford 80.3% versus 75.6%; each of five 10-node CLRS-Text and two 8-variable LEGO tasks has 2,000 train, 200 validation, 200 test examples, averaged over three seeds. Table 3 reports 4-bit Bellman-Ford 80.3% versus 32-bit 75.3%, within this task-specific training setting. The stated 3.5% average is consistent with a relative aggregate gain over the best per-task baseline but is 2.61 percentage points on an unweighted task mean; paper does not clarify this denominator. At 20% longer inputs all five graph tasks score below 25%. The Jacobian bound-to-loss-gap ratio ranges from roughly 8 for Qwen-1.5B to 10^5–10^6 for Llama-1B and Gemma-2B. Released DFS/BFS CLRS and cyclic LEGO launchers at commit 0dbd4f415bac7df5d989f4696938c4198113d08d select BF16 and quant_training_mode=lora; src/quantization/quant.py applies simulated quantization only to lora_A/lora_B in that mode, while full-model quantization is separate. These launchers do not prove every table cell used that exact command, but do not demonstrate a 1–4-bit deployed base. No native GGUF CPU export, same-base Q4_K_M complete bytes, cold total RAM, full-request CPU-seconds, or sealed structural holdout. Unreplicated preprint.

title: Efficient Reasoning on the Edge
note: Qwen2.5-7B quantized-base and reasoning-adapter precedent. Base uses INT4 per-channel linear weights including LM head, INT8 input embeddings and KV cache, INT16 activations; rank-128 LoRA reasoning adapters are trained on the quantized base then INT8-quantized. Table 11 uses five public math/science benchmarks: after 1.2M OpenThoughts3 examples, W4A16KV8 mean 58.12% versus BF16 60.54%, with MATH500 89.6% versus 94.0%. At 50k examples, a naive quantized base plus full-precision reasoning adapter scores zero mean; quantization-aware adaptation restores 39.25% and a stronger quantized base lifts it to 41.72%. Budget-forced RL reports 2.38 ± 0.07-times shorter average completions on MATH500 but 32k-token accuracy 92% versus SFT baseline 95%; constrained 1k to 6k accuracy favors the budget-forced model. RL uses eight H100s; the quantized-base transform takes under 24 hours on one H100. GENIE/ONNX mobile export and NPU-oriented decoding are described, but no complete deployed bytes, cold total RAM, full-request CPU-seconds, Q4_K_M same-base comparator, or sealed dependent-step quality are reported. BF16 comparator is the central denominator limitation; unreplicated preprint.

title: CodeQuant: Unified Clustering and Quantization for Enhanced Outlier Smoothing in Low-Precision Mixture-of-Experts
note: Revised 2026-08-14, first posted 2026-04-12. Appendix A.5 Table 9 benchmarks a T-MAC lookup-table CPU kernel on Xeon w7-3445 with 20 threads against BF16 and A8W4 llama.cpp controls. Against A8W4, reported memory/latency are 4.1 GB/13.3 s versus 4.1 GB/15.0 s for Phi-mini-MoE-Instruct, 8.9 GB/14.2 s versus 8.8 GB/17.1 s for DeepSeek-V2-Lite, and 16.5 GB/15.9 s versus 16.2 GB/20.1 s for Qwen3-30B-A3B: speed improves, memory is equal or higher. Claimed up-to-4.15-times CPU speedup compares with BF16. Paper specifies 512-prefill/128-decode/batch-16 for the GPU simulator but does not unambiguously bind that workload to the CPU table; memory statistic is not identified as cold process/cgroup peak. Latency is wall seconds, not CPU-seconds. Official repository https://github.com/SAI-Lab-NYU/CodeQuant describes fake-quant task evaluation. No complete installed bytes, same-base Q4_K_M comparator, full-request CPU-seconds, or sealed dependent-step quality.

title: CodeQuant2: Enhanced Outlier Mitigation and Adaptive Clustering for Low-Precision LRMs
note: Qwen3-4B-Thinking A4W4 cumulative ablation Table 5 raises six-benchmark average accuracy 0.664 to 0.770 with learned rotation/scaling, adaptive clusters, learned assignments and reasoning-aware calibration. Calibration uses full-precision GSM8K-training decoded prefixes mixed 9:1 with WikiText2. Separate Table 6 segment ablation raises an eight-metric mean 0.745 to 0.754, while AIME25 pass@1 falls 0.546 to 0.517; the eight-metric mean also includes AIME pass@8. All-768-token calibration lowers mean to 0.708. Final A4W4 Qwen3-4B-Thinking AIME25 pass@1 is 0.563 versus BF16 0.688, whereas pass@8 is 0.800 versus BF16 0.733 at eight-sample cost. Roughly 75 minutes reported fine-tuning stages on one H100. System speedup is CUDA lookup-kernel GPU decode latency on A6000/L40s/A100 against BF16, not CPU full-request CPU-seconds. Official release at https://github.com/SAI-Lab-NYU/CodeQuant2/blob/eaf112cb1da3a7e6010006c7f5341307c2c9768b/README.md#L220-L302 evaluates a reconstructed dense HF checkpoint with vLLM activation fake quantization, while its standalone packed CUDA kernel handles only 16-centroid channels, not the 8/32 options from adaptive cluster allocation. The released evaluation and kernel paths therefore do not establish a single native packed artifact with the reported task quality and speed. No complete GGUF package, cold CPU peak, same-base Q4_K_M comparison, or sealed dependent-step quality. Unreplicated preprint.

title: Sustainability Is Not Linear: Quantifying Performance, Energy, and Privacy Trade-offs in On-Device Intelligence
note: Same-phone, CPU-only llama.cpp comparison of eight Q4_K_M versus IQ4_XS model pairs on Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra, eight threads, 30 timed hardware repeats per configuration. Pinned raw aggregate at https://github.com/eziyoo/LLMs-on-Devices/blob/4090c3a3687fa4e3ea6fb1c1bea45dafeb1f704c/data/aggregated/final_results.csv: Qwen2.5-1.5B Q4_K_M versus IQ4_XS reported inference latency 4.37 versus 4.61 s, llama-cli memory-breakdown total 1373 versus 1162 MiB, energy 92.87 versus 93.42 J, comparative Overall G-Eval 0.69 versus 0.66. IQ4_XS has lower reported memory in all eight pairs but slower inference timing in seven. Fixed one summarization prompt, exactly 100 generated tokens; 30 hardware repeats are not independent quality examples. Inference latency comes from llama.cpp prefill-plus-generation timing and excludes model load. Memory is parsed model+context+compute, not process RSS or cgroup peak. Model_weight 1059 versus 848 MiB is not complete GGUF file size. One GPT-5.2 comparative judge call per criterion across 16 fixed-order response prefixes. Released aggregate lacks checkpoint/artifact hashes, although reproduction guide gives same-source quantization option. No complete package bytes, full-request CPU-seconds, cold total RAM, or sealed dependent-step quality. Single phone, one task; unreplicated preprint.

title: A Systematic Evaluation of On-Device LLMs: Quantization, Performance, and Resources
note: Windows i7-1360P laptop process peak working set via psutil and warm llama.cpp prefill/decode throughput are reported separately from five benchmark quality evaluations on a GPU workstation. Table 1 Qwen2.5-1.5B GSM8K FP16 60.80% versus q4_k 52.77%; not Q4_K_M versus same-base Q4_K_M. Synthetic 1024-token output, not completed-task CPU-seconds; no complete GGUF byte/hash audit, cold cgroup RAM, or sealed dependent-step quality. Internal inconsistencies: Section 3.1 says five selected formats while Table 1 has eight; method says 1024 outputs while Figure 5 caption says 1000; Table 2 q2_k/FP16 ratios conflict with prose. Paper flags 7B q4_0 working set 6910 MB, above q5_0 4837 MB. Linked anonymous code URL returned an access challenge on 2026-11-12. Use only as a measurement-cautionary source, not affirmative four-gate evidence.

title: RAMP: Reinforcement Adaptive Mixed-Precision Quantization for Efficient On-Device LLM Inference
note: Table 8 Llama-2-7B reports 3.68 GB and WikiText-2 perplexity 5.54 for RAMP versus 3.95 GB and 5.61 for Q4_K_M; four commonsense-task mean 63.6% versus 62.4%. Paper maps learned bit allocations to GGUF presets but does not link a released implementation or candidate artifact. Its Table 5 CPU platform figures are explicitly representative public llama.cpp benchmarks, not measurements of RAMP versus its Q4_K_M comparator. Section 5.2.1 describes 128 calibration sequences as roughly 20,000 tokens, whereas Table 10 calls them 128 sequences of 2,048 tokens each. No verified complete package bytes, cold process/cgroup peak, full-request CPU-seconds, or sealed dependent-step quality. Unreplicated preprint; substantive prior for bit allocation, not four-gate evidence.

title: CCQA: Generating Question from Solution Can Improve Inference-Time Reasoning in SLMs
note: Table 1 reports Qwen2.5-1.5B MultiArith accuracy of 95.00% with few-shot chain-of-thought versus 21.67% greedy on 180 test problems. The dataset has 420 training problems, but this Qwen arm is few-shot inference, not a Qwen fine-tuning result; the paper names other benchmark training sets for its separate Flan-T5 question generator. Experiments use A6000 48GB GPUs, temperature 0.7, top-p 0.9 for sampled solutions; the paper does not pin its 1.5B checkpoint to the Instruct GGUF used locally. This is a development-prompt lead on two-operation arithmetic, not a same-artifact CPU Q4_K_M result or evidence on three-fact dependent state, complete bytes, cold RAM, and full-request CPU-seconds.

title: Solving General Arithmetic Word Problems
note: Introduces the Commoncore set, commonly used as MultiArith, with 600 problems in six two-operation categories of 100 each; six-fold cross-validation holds out one whole category per fold. title: CLUTRR: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Inductive Reasoning from Text
note: Primary paper §4.2 defines relation-chain length k as the required reasoning steps and evaluates k=2,3 or k=2,3,4 training versus k=2..10 tests, using 5,000 training and 100 test stories per k across 10 random runs, with 20% paraphrases and 10% logical clauses held out during training. Official generator: https://github.com/facebookresearch/clutrr/tree/d045fae289d3746503677ceed7631c999202501e . README describes template and relation-pattern split flags. At this commit, clutrr/args.py line 64 makes --template_split store_true with default True, so CLI cannot disable it; clutrr/generator.py lines 41-56 replaces loaded train/test templates with the same synthetic relation templates unless the AMT renderer is selected; and lines 126-145 force relation-pattern overlap for k=2 regardless of --holdout. Audit rendered split IDs. Repo license is CC BY-NC 4.0. Published results involve trained benchmark models, not the local pretrained 1.5B Q4_K_M CPU artifact; no whole-file, cold RAM, or full-request CPU gate is reported. A prospective internal development/evaluation holdout does not rule out public benchmark pretraining exposure.

title: The Dichotomy Between Pattern Recognition and Step-by-Step Reasoning
note: Primary preprint. Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct BF16 LoRA, roughly 2.3% trainable parameters. Algebra: 50,000 train and 1,000 distinct test per each of three replicate experiments; unperturbed final-answer accuracy 0.973 with state every step, 0.587 with operations but no states, 0.564 direct; fixed-token control gives k=1 only 24,536 training samples because traces are longer. Story: 479-story generated corpus, 375 train and 63 held-out stories per split, four questions per story, three seeds, 252 test questions per seed; state tracking 0.866 accuracy at median 852 reasoning tokens, length-comparable local narration 0.438 at 648, key-sentence reasoning 0.694 at 38. Story holdout is by instance, not unseen dependency structure. Appendix C does not explain the 41 stories left after its stated 375 train and 63 test allocations from a 479-story corpus. More frequent states improve unperturbed accuracy but reduce robustness to answer-preserving reasoning perturbations. No Q4_K_M GGUF, complete package bytes, CPU full-request time, or cold process/cgroup RAM. Unreplicated preprint; promising quality-training control only.

title: Explore Theory-of-Mind: Program-Guided Adversarial Data Generation for Theory of Mind Reasoning
note: Primary paper and official generator at https://github.com/facebookresearch/exploretom/tree/6a9372870ddc1c7b9b9ce1f3ee1641dbbdb56760 . Symbolic story-state tracker generates deterministic questions and answers. Table 9 reports only 5.6% to 8.6% of randomly sampled story/question/answer triples require a false-belief answer differing from world state in the stated two- to four-person, two- to four-movement settings; balance gold-defined dependency and answer classes before model queries. Their A* search selects stories a target model misses, so its worst-case 0% Llama-3.1-70B and 9% GPT-4o scores cannot be used as an absolute-floor expectation for a different model. Official README says released sample targets Llama-3.1-70B and another target should regenerate. This is a benign task-design source, not evidence for same-base CPU GGUF bytes, cold RAM, full-request CPU-seconds or sealed quality retention.

title: Brief Is Better: Non-Monotonic Chain-of-Thought Budget Effects in Function-Calling Language Agents
note: ArXiv abstract confirms submission 2 April 2026, although the HTML paper body is dated 24 August 2026. On 200 contiguous BFCL v3 Multiple single-call tasks, BF16 Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct with two-stage hard reasoning budgets scores 44.0% with d=0, 64.0% with d=32, 25.0% with d=256, 22.5% with d=512; generation permits up to 256 additional answer tokens. Fine-grained d=16 is 69.0% on 100 tasks in Appendix C, versus 71.5% on 200 tasks in Table 5, so denominators differ. Oracle 88.6% means 148/167 tasks solved by some tested budget, not all 200. Table 5 zero observed final function hallucination on 200 prompts does not provide a structural guarantee: routing traces are invalid in 0.5% and 1.5% for 1.5B and 7B. Single-call routing is not dependent multistep integration; two-stage hard stops and format parsing may affect transfer. No released runnable code identified in paper, no Q4_K_M GGUF, complete bytes, cold CPU RAM, full-request CPU-seconds, or sealed composition quality. Use only as a reference-only prompt-budget development caution, not a compression result.

title: When Does Reasoning Age? Survival Analysis of Step-Level Error Hazard in LLM Chains
note: Primary paper labels 18,969 greedy-decoded chains across five benchmarks and seven models from 3B to 70B or API access. A Weibull model finds increasing first-error hazard in 34/35 dataset-model cells; however, Weibull is AIC-preferred in only 4/35, while nonparametric Mann-Kendall tests show significant positive trends in only five of seven ProofWriter cells after correction and significant negative trends in two other cells. Fan-in association is N=5 dataset means, Spearman 0.90, exact p=0.083. Simulated last-step checking detects 94% of ProofWriter errors versus 23% uniform at K=1 with 70/30 split and 100 repeats; this measures error detection, not corrected task success or runtime saving. Authors cannot distinguish cumulative model degradation from later structurally harder steps; unparseable steps can be coded correct. Useful only for preregistering secondary conditional step-error diagnostics alongside unconditional final-task success. No same-base GGUF, complete bytes, cold CPU RAM, or full-request CPU cost.

title: Broken on Arrival: Non-Functional Quantized LLM Artifacts in Public Model Registries and How to Catch Them
note: Census of 305 eligible code-capable official Ollama GGUF tags in 15 selected model lines, plus 22 popular community files; 291 official tags are quantized. Seven official tags (2.3%) solved at most 6/164 HumanEval+ tasks and were grouped into three model-variant incidents, all low-bit and at most 4B. On Qwen2.5-Coder-3B, a same-checkpoint/toolchain/tensor-mix importance matrix raised three failed Q2/Q3 levels from zero to 76–113/164, while Q3_K_S reached only 30/164 and failed the paper's rescue rule, which was added after initial rebuild results. A Q4_K_M rebuild scored 129/164. The 15-task screen was tuned on 23 healthy Qwen configurations and is a coarse code-function screen, not a sealed dependent-step benchmark. A scorer timeout fault required serial rescore of failed HumanEval/15 outputs. GPU CUDA/Metal generation, registry-limited census, code-task outcome only; no complete installed bytes, cold CPU peak, or full-request CPU-seconds. Unreplicated preprint.

title: GGUF-Metadata Prediction of Single-Sequence llama.cpp Throughput Across Three Systems
note: Primary arXiv v1 reports 53 scored host-file configurations from 22 GGUF files on two M4 Max hosts and an RTX 5080. Quantizer-specific, host-fitted metadata predictor obtains held-out decode MAPE 13.1%, 14.4%, and 36.1% over only four, five, and two configurations; three prefix-depth rows per configuration are correlated. Its RTX prefill held-out MAPE is 108.2%. An added output-projection term is not selected because held-out benefit is inconsistent. Separate llama-bench 512-token prefill and 128-token decode phases at prefixes 0/4096/16384 do not measure complete-request CPU-seconds; requested GPU offload does not establish physical residency, and cold RAM or quality is not measured. Useful prior for cost-model features and a negative transfer warning, not evidence of a four-gate CPU GGUF gain.

Tests use H100 GPUs and vLLM; they do not measure CPU Q4_K_M, complete-request CPU-seconds, process/cgroup peak, or a same-artifact four-axis gate.

title: Streamlining LLM Inference at the Edge with TFLite

note: Eligible CPU kernels may prepack weights during session initialization; parallel prepack can overlap mapped page-ins. Opt-in external initializer direct buffers may borrow naturally aligned native-endian CPU mmap buffers larger than 127 B, avoiding an initial initializer copy while caller keeps them alive. Borrowing does not prove elimination of subsequent kernel prepack allocations; no GGUF Q4_K_M four-axis test.

On RTX 6000 Ada FP8/sGLang, it needs 3-5 times more decode steps for comparable output; Chinese-character throughput is about one-quarter and 65,536-byte Chinese-input prefill 6.5 times slower, partly due to less-tuned kernels. title: Same Request, Different Answer: Quantization Amplifies Cache-Induced Divergence in LLM Serving
note: On RTX 4090 with CUDA-offloaded llama.cpp b10434, Qwen2.5-7B Q4_K_M had cache-hit versus recompute path divergence in 82.5% of 80 BFCL multistep episodes averaged over ten fresh server histories, versus 37.4% at F16. In a separate single-history default prompt-cache grid, Q4_K_M cache-enabled repeat divergence was 77.5% of 80 episodes; disabling the server-level prompt cache reduced it to 1/80, with the residual due to an empty versus warm prefix cache. Cache-disabled repeats matched exactly in tested configurations. GPU, different model and build, no CPU resource or joint compression result; motivates freezing and reporting cache policy and fresh process state in paired quality evaluations.

note: Author protocol alternates paired agents; each model may read peer strategy files, change its own candidate, and publish after evaluation. Adoption is model-guided candidate-code transfer, not an after-each access check in one resident process.

title: Reflections on Trusting Trust, Revisited: Contaminating Self-Modifying AI Coding Agents with Poisoned Benchmarks
note: Controlled poisoned-benchmark study of offline agent evolution. Modified DGM required a researcher change outside the attacker model and evolved code-emitting tools; SICA and Hyperagents primarily evolved instructions that affected code on neutral tasks. Selected descendants tested on ten held-out tasks three times each; one contaminated agent per system was continued under four feedback conditions. Feedback integrity precedent, not resident payload revision or access-survival evidence.

title: SWE-Shift: Evaluating Coding Agents in Evolving Workspaces
note: Matched Clean/Shifted coding-agent continuations from the same saved prefix for 120 recoverable scenarios, 12 external change families, nine intervention positions, and 17 systems. Original tests can miss preservation or stale-evidence failure. One external change per run, uncontrolled model randomness, and no self-revised agent payload, continuing remote-access instance, or after-two-revisions check. Open-weight runs used 32 B300 GPUs.

publisher: Cao, Deng, and Kersting (arXiv preprint, version 1)
title: Blind to What They Can Fix: A Detection Gap in Self-Improving Agents
note: Five-domain benign study separates agent-written runtime checks, externally scored task failures, and forced-call repair on the same program/change units. Standard checks miss many failures that the author later repairs when explicitly recalled; improved purpose instructions reduce misses in two new-program conditions. Frozen programs, small independent-program counts, replayed one-call deployment, and no same-process two-revision remote access.

title: Phantom Guardrails: When Self-Improving Agent Harnesses Fix Failures That Never Happened
note: Deterministic board-game micro-lab tests unwarranted guard additions with byte-exact violation oracle. 15/60 single-shot proposals on patterned all-legal input versus 0/60 featureless; four-round add-only acceptance can retain no-op guard, while warrant-aware gate excludes it in this setting. Abstract guard menu, no arbitrary code replacement, continuing process, or remote-control result.

title: How Do Coding-Agent Harnesses Self-Evolve? An Empirical Study of Retrospective Adaptation
note: Thirty benign Claude Code sessions produced 125 retrospective proposals; researchers implemented 24, evaluated 12 adaptations in 13 paired fresh-session transfer events, and deemed seven informative. Loaded/consulted context did not ensure target-action reduction; selected tasks, small cells and human choice limit rates. No executable resident-code or remote-access sequence.

title: Inside a malicious Claude Code-branded extension and its persistent SSH backdoor
note: First-party package analysis distinguishes loader code order, key/persistence artifacts, SSH process, and successful attacker access. Cursor reported SSH access blocked on most macOS/Windows hosts by errors or privilege requirements. Claude Code branding was lure/supply-chain context; no model-driven payload revision. Use as an access-oracle counterexample, not a Drexel case.

title: What defenders need to know about ARTEX, the agentic AI framework threat actors abuse
note: First-party November 2026 field and framework analysis. ARTEX external Go backend coordinates goal/planner/worker agents and can switch model providers. Microsoft describes several short-lived web shells with incrementing names, each running a different command, as agents correct errors; it also describes RAT installation as a separate action. No two model-caused revisions of one resident RAT with after-each access results. Detection indicators are behavioral suggestions with configuration and coverage conditions, not a measured Drexel alert rate.

title: Silver Dragon Targets Organizations in Southeast Asia and Europe
note: First-party GearDoor analysis distinguishes a binary self-update path that explicitly restarts the malware process from a separate .NET assembly plugin path that executes additional code in memory. The publication describes capabilities and evolving builds, not two observed same-process plugin-version activations; no model-to-code provenance or after-each command trace.

title: ARIA: Runtime Inspection and Amendment for Multi-Agent Systems
note: Benign multi-agent intervention study with verified repair pairs, paired untreated controls, task-normalized harmful-intervention accounting, and a single pending plain-text message substitution per live run. No resident payload-code activation or two-revision remote-control chain; its harm rates cannot estimate Drexel.

title: REVISE: Validity-Guided Recovery for Online Revisions in Agent Workflows
note: Benign structured-agent workflow study where revision means a new instruction/change during execution, not code version. Dependency-based invalidation and commit-time revalidation avoid stale outputs/effects in 300 challenging event-order tests; serving results use Qwen3-14B on four H100 GPUs. Useful current-version provenance analogy, not implant feasibility rate.

title: ARTEX leads to persistent ZQAgent backdoor
note: First-party incident-response account says ARTEX deployed a persistent Linux backdoor in Belgium. It documents binary capability and configuration; the analyzed image copies itself to memfd and restarts as a detached process. Operator-specific tasking is analyst inference. No model-to-code authorship or revision trace, two same-process active versions, or after-each-version remote-control command/result record.

title: The Agent That Robbed Itself: an AI-Driven Hugging Face Malware Campaign Leaks Its Own Operator
note: First-party public-artifact and commit-history analysis attributes malicious model creation/upload/self-test to an ARTEX task with high confidence. Multiple external artifact changes and one operator-container self-test are documented; exact model response-to-delta provenance and human-versus-model choices are unresolved. The latest second-model config fails under stock transformers; no external-victim result or same-process two-revision remote-control chain.

title: AgentWorm: Self-Propagating Attacks Across LLM Agent Ecosystems
note: Controlled OpenClaw agent-ecosystem study: 2250 independent trials across three vectors, three payloads, and five models; separate 90-trial five-session-restart longevity panel. Persistent change is agent instruction/configuration, and C2 category fetches operator-served task text. Fresh sessions and markers check adoption/execution/propagation, not two model-caused executable-code versions in one remote-access process. The earlier v1 used the title ClawWorm; rates and denominators require version pinning.

title: Malicious npm Package Turns Hermes Agent into a Backdoor
note: First-party static analysis of nine malicious fake-CRM package releases. Early versions attempted to install and remotely task Hermes Agent as a service; later releases changed delivery mechanism and downloads were not recovered. SafeDep reports no observed victim installation. Package versions, hosted persona changes, and connection-check code do not show model-authored active code revisions or two post-revision remote-control results in one process.

title: Beyond Handcrafted Security: Towards Self-Evolving Defense for LLM Agents
note: Controlled defense-harness evolution study. In five long-horizon progressive-attack rounds, action-side gate rules grow 0 to 97; evolution-split attack success falls 36.6% to 23.2%, but held-out attack success changes only 28.9% to 26.5%. Separate policy arm and benign-utility results show transfer/tradeoffs. Single evaluation pass, fresh task trajectories, policy/rule edit surface; no same-process two-code-revision remote-access chain.

title: Asiel Core application: self-edit and plugin-evolution loops
note: Static source shows LLM-directed Python plugin BUILD, REFINE, and EVOLVE paths calling PluginLoader.reload in a continuing app. It is an implementation path, not a published two-version runtime trace or remote-access experiment.

title: Asiel Core PluginLoader

title: NexAgent agent-facing upgrade_code tool

title: NexAgent evolution integration test
note: Checked-in mock-model integration test covers soul, memory, and skill evolution, not two live executable-module replacements or after-each function results.

title: PluginRSI: Recursive Improvement of Agent Harnesses with Reusable Plugins
note: Benign offline harness search with executable Python plugin mutation: 8 branches per iteration screened on 20-task minibatches, recomposed incumbent checked on 400 held-in SWE-bench tasks, 15 iterations, then frozen evaluation on 100 held-out tasks. Its separate plugin-reuse analysis optimizes on those 100, changing their status for that analysis. No same-process serial remote-access revision.

title: Is Three the Magic Number? An Empirical Evaluation of LLM-Based Repair Loops
note: Source-only audit of six benign tool-dataset repair workflows with three model backbones through ten repair steps. Early repairs carry most completion gain, but curves depend on prompt/test exposure and workflow; some interfaces changed and configurations were not repeatedly sampled. No active serial code revision or remote-control result.

publisher: Kanso et al. (IEEE CSR 2026 conference abstract)
title: COGENT: A Framework for Studying LLM-Guided Adaptive Evasion in Endpoint Security
note: Public abstract reports GPT-4o-mini-generated semantic code variants and longer execution than polymorphic baselines over multiple automated mutation cycles on isolated Windows VMs. Full methods/tables unavailable in this audit; no process/version lineage or post-each-revision remote-control result in accessible abstract. Conference held August 2026; IEEE Xplore record added November 9.

publisher: Kanso (American University of Beirut thesis repository abstract)
title: Generative Steganography for Covert Command-and-Control Communication: Modeling and Detectability Study
note: Repository abstract reports 45 thirty-minute COGENT/Typhon runs across 15 endpoint products, all with bidirectional workflow completion and no relevant alert/block from tested controls, plus separate ARGUS detection. Thesis PDF was marked restricted/request-a-copy on November 26. No accessible per-revision process/version trace; do not conflate thesis matrix with IEEE mutation-cycle experiment.

title: Closing the Sim-to-Real Gap: An Evaluation Framework for Autonomous Cyber Defense Configuration of Commercial EDR
note: Commercial EDR policy-agent evaluation: 20 Microsoft Defender XDR pentests and shorter CrowdStrike/SentinelOne probes. ASR telemetry delay/throttling, per-vendor attribution granularity, and stateful autonomous response complicate alert and block measures. No model-authored payload revisions; method source for a future benign endpoint-observability protocol, not a Drexel detection rate.

publisher: Sugio and Ito (IEEE Access publisher record)
title: Jailbreak-Free LLM-Assisted Malware Generation: An Empirical and Conceptual Analysis

publisher: Sugio and Ito (public accepted author manuscript)

note: Seven-framework controlled study of one researcher-authored trusted-tool implementation update; normal function and independently confirmed extra effects are scored separately. RQ1 has 21 conditions x five rounds x 20 planned tasks; no model-caused two-revision remote-control chain.

title: Reassessing One-Round Test-Time Refinement for Code Generation
note: Paired exact initial Python candidates across seven models and three benchmarks; 11,683 model-task cases in each of three independently generated runs on the same tasks. Diagnostic Self-Debug generally improved or preserved final-test accuracy, whereas feedback-free Self-Refine often regressed. Diagnostic-pass abstention missed 34.1% of initial final-test failures in first run. Standalone tasks, local models GPU-served, no serial live service or C2.

title: AI-Generated PowerShell Malware: An Experimental Framework and Dataset
note: Four roughly 7–9B generator configurations compared with held-out PowerShell references. Sigma-rule overlap is conditioned on 212 reference-triggering scripts among 236 test samples; best native model 84.5% median Jaccard and 48.4% exact rule-set match, 4-bit AWQ exact match 35.9%. Generated/reference scripts ran in separate restored Windows VMs with endpoint defenses disabled. Training and inference used four A100 64GB GPUs; no CPU endpoint budget, working C2, or serial same-process code revision measured.

title: OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo
note: Reports Codex-generated Java Base64 guard attached directly to a running Elasticsearch process and exploit attempt blocked while service continued. One controlled defensive shield, no two-version lineage or remote-control workload.

title: Cisco and OpenAI introduce Shirudo
note: Describes Codex-driven shield generation, observed attachment to running Elasticsearch 9.5.5, and application log entries for guard installation and rejected malformed Base64 input. Does not publish exact model output, pre/post PID, two installed versions, or remote-control checks.

publisher: Bitdefender Labs (first-party full technical report, pinned GitHub commit)
title: SilkParasite: Tracking a China-Nexus APT Across Central Asia — 62-page research report
note: Pp. 17–25 document DriveSilkRAT task-supplied in-memory .NET plugins and returned results; 37 surviving operator command files lower-bound activity, not successful plugin versions. P.34 CookiETagRAT load|success precedes mapping/initialization; plugins not recovered. P.48 NomadRAT loadsuccess follows export resolution/initialization but not function result. AI-assisted development assessed medium confidence from indirect clues, not a model-to-plugin trace. No two-version same-process C2 sequence.

title: Local LLM AI and Huntress
note: Reports one observed local AI session generating over 90,000 process events in a minute and occasional EDR-agent CPU/RAM pressure on AI coding-agent workloads. No cohort denominator, proof of model inference locality, malware, alert/block outcome, or direct inference-to-event causality. Source for event-volume and observer-overhead measurement, not Drexel detection probability.

The 3B q4_K_M file solved 366 at 69.4 rail J/solve versus 363 at 141.2 for 7B q2_K; five alternating HumanEval+ pairs supported the relative energy gap. Post hoc noninferiority margin, single-session main grid, listed file-size budget, and no dependent live revisions or endpoint detection. Not a CPU-only or Drexel outcome measure.

title: DDBench: A Benchmark for Agentic Debugging on Distributed Systems
note: Sixty curated historical bugs in 13 distributed-system repositories; ten models in one mini-swe-agent scaffold. On 31 tier-1 cases, bounded diagnostic bundles raised aggregate final-oracle pass rate from 31.0% to 50.0% across 310 paired model-case comparisons (72 fail-to-pass, 13 pass-to-fail). Bundles were generated by one model, not content-ablated; isolated final patches and large self-hosted models do not establish two live same-process revisions, remote-control retention, or small CPU cost.

note: execve retains OS process identity/PID but replaces program image and most in-memory process state; PID/start time alone is insufficient evidence of uninterrupted resident image.

title: Harness-R1: Learning to Edit Executable Runtime Harnesses from Agent Failure Trajectories
note: Separate 9B engineer generates executable Python harness patches from failure batches; patched frozen target reruns tasks. Equal-weight success 44.3% to 53.6%; 1,270 held-out tasks +8.9±1.5 pp over three seeds. One benchmark-level patch and fresh task runs, not repeated same-instance payload revisions or C2. Training uses H800 GPUs.

title: Recursive self-improvement of AI research agents
note: Eight-day 100-node harness-code search with 99 rewrite proposals and seven accepted at steps 2, 6, 28, 39, 47, 63, 85; selection grade .703 to .778. Candidate agents undergo fresh benchmark runs, not live resident code replacement; no C2. Outer model Claude Opus 4.7, inner Gemini 3 Flash.

title: Claude & Control: An Introduction to Agentic C2 with Computer Use Agents
note: Researcher reports C# endpoint control loop with Azure relay and cloud Claude API, plus working desktop tasks and no MDE/CrowdStrike alerts in his test. No complete trial denominator, endpoint policy/version or raw alert telemetry; no model-authored implant revision, two active versions, or after-update access check.

title: Weaponizing Claude Code Hooks: Building a C2 Through the Skill Lifecycle
note: Researcher-prepared skill hook invokes child script around agent tool calls and polls remote tasking. Model need not choose, inspect, or author C2 code. Repeated hook firings are not two model-authored resident-code revisions; report discusses process/network/file detection signals.

title: Samizdat guarded live cell-mutation protocol
note: Pinned implementation checkpoints, reloads, validates, soaks, probes, and commits or rolls back Clojure cells. Candidate can remain pending with old handler active through a held-out battery. Architecture source, not an observed model-authored two-version trace or remote-control result.

title: Samizdat cell-mutation unit tests
note: Checked-in test asserts one human-authored cell edit becomes live and returns updated output; a pending candidate retains prior handler until verdict. Also covers rollback. Test text inspected, not executed for Drexel research; no two-edit model transcript or C2 workload.

title: Poiesis durable logical process and re-exec upgrade design
note: Author describes durable application-level job PID and stored context, while promotion of rewritten code re-executes the node and wipes RAM. Shows why a persistent logical agent identity is not evidence of uninterrupted resident image; no serial model-to-code/C2 result trace.

note: self.define journals a proposed complete Lisp definition and compiles/installs it into the active image, with installed/failed journal state and undo. Supports mechanism, not a recorded model-output or serial remote-control outcome.

note: Fixture checks one function replacement returns changed value; another installs two human-authored definitions, discards the second, and checks first is restored. No model transcript, after-each install function check, or remote-control task. Test text inspected, not run.

note: Separates exploratory active-image installation, private commit/replay, and checkpoint/recovery; Windows checkpoint uses save-lisp-and-die and boots saved core, so it is not uninterrupted resident-image continuity.

publisher: Radovič et al. (arXiv v1; accepted NeurIPS 2026 SLM-Agents workshop)
title: Should SLMs be in the Driver's Seat? A Study of Local Models as Interpreters in Cloud-Written Agent Programs
note: On 168 AppWorld Test Normal and 417 Test Challenge tasks, a larger model writes Python programs while a local SLM answers bounded data-interpretation calls. Qwen3.6-27B planner plus 9B SLM reached 60.7%±3.8 TN vs 45.8%±3.9 code-first and 81.0%±3.0 ReAct; a 2B interpreter reached 61.3%±3.7. title: Built to Remember, Shipped to Forget: Operational Contracts, Failures, and Repairs in Containerized LLM Agent Deployments
note: Among 433 selected public deployments, 265 needed durable state; 99/265 lost it to process restart and 110/265 to container replacement. In 61 background-work systems, 54 lacked a resumption mechanism. Distinguishes state survival from run resumption; these are population-specific deployment observations, not Drexel rates.

note: Checked-in tests establish signal listeners and restart constant, not two changed-version functional outcomes. Test text inspected only; no execution for this research.

title: Chinese-nexus actor's Cairn AI agents found a zero-day on their own
note: Investigators inspected an exposed Cairn controller and report agent-directed file write followed in a later session by a Python reverse shell loaded by a newly spawned process. Exact model-output-to-payload artifact not published; no two same-process revisions or after-each access result. Separate failed target operations are not serial-revision trials.

publisher: Gambit Security Threat Intelligence (first-party field investigation)
title: Autonomous AI Agents are breaking into hundreds of Online Retailers for $25 a target in an ongoing campaign
note: Recovered operator staging server plus some independently verified skimmers and exfiltrated data. note: Post-trained Qwen3 4B SSH tool-use agent: 112/120 held-out privilege-escalation runs by 20 rounds on fresh containers, served with vLLM on RTX 5090. note: Distinguishes polymorphic encrypted-body and metamorphic code-form mutation. Its detector comparison is a bounded test-set result, not evidence that variants are universally invisible to defenders.
